newsitem.title: CANADA: Asian millers seek higher protein and gluten wheat.
newsitem.headline: Asian millers seek higher protein and gluten wheat.

text.p: Asia's largest millers said Friday they need higher quantity protein and gluten in Canada's best know Canada Western Red Spring (CWRS) wheat.

"Japan imports No1 CWRS and it's the best for bread making but recently the quality and protein is slightly down and we hope we'll see more stable protein performance in baking," said Hiroki Kimura, leader of Japan's Showa Sangyo Co Ltd wheat science and technology group.
Flour's value depends on quantity and quality of protein. Water added to wheat protein forms gluten.
Gluten retain gas allowing dough to rise. The more water flour can absorb will yield more dough and produce more bread.
"It (No1 CWRS) is slightly below 13 percent (protein), it's still very good, but it could be better," Kimura told Reuters while on a wheat evaluation seminar in Winnipeg.
Although Canada boasts having some of the highest quality wheat in the world, the grain's protein quantity was at issue.

"The baking qualities are not as good as (U.S.) DNS (Dark Northern Spring wheat) which has stronger gluten properties," said Gwanchai Leangprasirt, quality assurance assistant manager of Thailand's United Floud Mill Public Co Ltd.
Canada is the second largest supplier of wheat to the world market after the United States.
The Canadian Wheat Board earned C$3.8 billion in crop year 1995/96 (Aug/July) on sales of 16 million tonnes of wheat.
Asian millers bought 9.1 million tonnes of CWB wheat in that period, CWB statistics show.
The millers suggested Canada or the CWB establish a formal process whereby end users can track grain shipments from primary elevators through to its final destination.
"There's no way to match a railcar report with a vessel report," said Lim Kay Kong, of Prima Flour Mills Ltd.

"We look for predictability in grain quality specifications because we don't always get consistent functionality and there's no mechanism to address this to mitigate our losses in competitiveness and Singapore is a very competitive market," Prima's manager of research and development said.
Prima also owns flour mills in Sri Lanka.
"The (Canadian) Wheat Board has offices in Beijing and Tokyo but it may be in their interests to open an office in southeast Asia," he added.
